thread: maya: FYI linkcheck failed after the MD migration. Several anchors with inline code or special chars now 404. Example: /docs/cli#add-user@role -> 404. docs-ci: linkcheck job failed: https://ci.internal/jobs/5012 (3 broken anchors) tony: I saw this pattern. Old slugify kept `@` and `.`; new slugify strips them and collapses punctuation, so migrated links point to non-canonical slugs. zhen: can we run a pass that recalculates canonical slugs from headings and rewrites internal links? That should be safe and idempotent. maya: yes, but watch i18n comments and any manual anchors. We should add an id-fallback for safety: insert `` right after the heading when slug rewriting is applied. tony: I'll prototype a small migration script: parse markdown headings, generate slug with the current slugify rules, find internal links pointing to the old slug and rewrite them. Also add a dry-run flag and create a backup tar. docs-ci: opened issue https://issues.internal/2378 for slug reconciliation. Also suggested adding a docs-ci static check that builds a tiny fixture site and asserts linkcheck == 0. zhen: good call. Add unit tests: variations include code spans, parentheses, at-signs, and trailing punctuation. tony: PR opened: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/942 (WIP). Includes script + tests + CI job. preview-bot: preview build for fix/slug-reconcile (PR 942) succeeded: https://preview.docs.internal/942 (linkcheck green) docs-ci: migration run produced backup: gs://internal/migrations/slug-reconcile-2026-03-23.tar.gz maya: reviewed and left tiny comments about logging and a note for translators. Once merged we'll run across all docs and monitor linkcheck for a day. tony: done, addressed comments. Merging after a short hold window. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
